parts.text:
Impulses travel between neurones across a synapse.
Describe how impulses travel across the synapse from one neurone to another.

parts.label: (c)
parts.text:
Drugs such as heroin restrict the movement of impulses across synapses. Users can become
addicted to heroin. When users stop taking heroin they may experience withdrawal symptoms.

parts.label: (i)
parts.text: State two withdrawal symptoms that heroin users may experience.

parts.label: (ii)
parts.text: Suggest why heroin abuse may increase criminal activity.

parts.label: (d)
parts.text:
Heroin abuse may lead to HIV infection. There is currently no approved vaccine that prevents
the spread of HIV. Vaccination stimulates active immunity against specific pathogens.

parts.label: (i)
parts.text: Explain how vaccination stimulates active immunity.

parts.label: (ii)
parts.text: Explain what is meant by passive immunity.

text: Reflexes are simple responses that protect the body.
The pathway that nerve impulses travel along during a reflex is called a reflex arc.

parts.label: (d)
parts.text:
Mechanically digested food travels from the mouth to the stomach. The gastric juice in the
stomach contains hydrochloric acid, giving a low pH environment.
Explain why it is important to have a low pH in the stomach.

parts.label: (e)
parts.text:
Products of digestion are absorbed through the villi in the small intestine.
Explain how villi are adapted for absorption.

parts.label: (f)
parts.text:
Coeliac disease is caused by a reaction to a protein called gluten. The villi become damaged
causing a reduction in the absorption of nutrients.
Suggest possible effects on the body of a reduction in the absorption of nutrients.
